title: sitesolide, deploy small apps to one server you own
excerpt: Internal tools, dashboards and prototypes, live on HTTPS behind your company's sign-in, on one server you own. Open source, MIT.
content_html:
Deploying, signing in, sharing, background work, backups and monitoring come built in, on a machine you own.

  • Deploy in one command

    Run sitesolide deploy in a folder: a static site, or an app in Bun, Node, Python, Go or any binary. It builds, installs, restarts, then checks the app answers on HTTPS.

  • A server you own

    One machine you rent, at Hetzner or any Debian 13 server. Caddy serves every app on HTTPS, at its own subdomain or on your domain, and systemd runs them. Apps, data and secrets stay on it: no containers, no per‑seat bill.

  • Your company's sign-in

    Google Workspace, Entra, Okta or any OpenID Connect provider in front of private apps, which write no sign-in code and learn who came in.

  • Shared like a doc

    Open an app to a colleague by their work email, or to everyone at your domain, from the CLI or the dashboard. It holds from their next request.

  • Team tokens, not root SSH

    Colleagues and agents deploy over HTTPS with a personal token, scoped and revoked in one click. Only the owner holds SSH.

  • Workers and schedules

    An agent that looks for leads around the clock, a report every weekday at eight: declare them in sitesolide.json beside the app. systemd brings a worker back when it falls and runs each schedule on time, and the sites keep the processor first.

  • Hourly backups

    Each project's data snapshotted hourly, SQLite copied consistently, optionally to an encrypted bucket. Restore from the dashboard.

  • Built for agents

    Every command speaks --json, one event per line, each error with a hint. sitesolide mcp serves deploy, logs and access to Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, and llms.txt indexes the docs.

  • A monitor that tells you

    Every site checked each minute: one message to Slack, Discord, Google Chat or ntfy when it goes down, one when it recovers. A heartbeat notices the machine itself dying.

Different tools for different jobs: a hosted cloud, a dashboard for containers, a container deploy tool.

Sources: each project's own site and docs, checked on 5 October 2026.

  • Vercel: no on-premise product, Dockerfiles supported, not required, CLI install, Passport, Pro plan
  • Coolify: installation, Docker, CLI, basic auth, pricing, license
  • Kamal: installation, proxy options, license
  • Out of date? Open an issue.

Once the CLI is installed: a domain on Cloudflare, and a Hetzner Cloud token or any Debian 13 server you reach as root.

  1. Order a machine

    or bring any Debian 13 server

    sitesolide machine create --provider hetzner --name web

  2. Install sitesolide on it

    hardened, DNS, Caddy, dashboard

    sitesolide setup root@203.0.113.10 --zone example.com --email you@example.com

  3. Deploy a project

    live at my-app.example.com

    cd my-app && sitesolide deploy

Read the docs What each step checks and changes
